item.title: Colombia's president backs Abascal: "Spain deserves a president like you"
item.description: Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella has backed Vox leader Santiago Abascal ahead of Sunday's general election in Spain, in a video Abascal himself shared on X on Friday, the last day of campaigning. "Dear friend, Spain deserves a president like you," the Colombian president said.

item.title: Spain wraps up its campaign: Sánchez appeals for a "progressive majority", Feijóo for "change"
item.description: The main candidates in Spain's snap general election on Sunday closed their campaigns on Friday with packed rallies, at which Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez appealed for a "progressive majority" and People's Party leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo even asked left-wing voters to back "change". The latest published polls gave the PP and Vox a combined majority.

item.title: Milei wins Senate approval to suspend primaries, with debates mandatory only in a run-off
item.description: Argentina's Senate on Thursday approved, by 43 votes to 29, the political reform promoted by Javier Milei's government that suspends the open, simultaneous and mandatory primary elections (PASO) ahead of the 2027 presidential election. The bill, which also limits mandatory presidential debates to a run-off, now goes to the Chamber of Deputies.

item.title: Argentina bans online betting advertising, including in football and on social media
item.description: Argentina's Senate unanimously passed, by 72 votes, a law to prevent gambling addiction and regulate online betting, banning gambling advertising in the media, on social media, in stadiums and on billboards, and requiring football clubs to review their sponsorship deals with betting firms. The law, approved on Thursday, had been pending in the upper house for more than two years.

item.title: All hostages rescued after Colombian security forces storm supermarket, police say
item.description:
Unclear if ‘hostage-taker’ who was killed may have been a hostage as daylong siege in Cartagena shopping centre ends

Colombian police have stormed a supermarket in one of the country’s most popular tourist cities, ending a daylong siege in which all the hostages were freed and one man police described as a hostage-taker was killed.

Abelardo de la Espriella, the far-right president, travelled to the Caribbean port city of Cartagena to follow the final hours of negotiations and the tactical assault, in which special forces officers broke through blocked entrances and detonated stun grenades.

item.title: How datacentres are driving an illegal mining rush in the Amazon ‘more devastating than gold’
item.description:
As demand for tin ores pushes up prices, criminal gangs are exploiting Indigenous lands and weak regulation to profit from Brazil’s abundant cassiterite

While searching for documents tied to an illegal cassiterite export network last September, Brazilian federal police officers were surprised to find a link between an illegal mining and money-laundering scheme and an address connected to one of Brazil’s biggest showbusiness stars from the 90s.

Alexandre Pires, a popular pagode singer-songwriter, is now under investigation as part of Operation Disco de Ouro (Gold Disc) for his alleged involvement in a scheme to illegally ship cassiterite worth millions of dollars abroad. During the investigation, police uncovered a message in which his agent, Matheus Possebon, allegedly admitted to his participation and said that he failed to deliver the illegal ore he had promised his associates.

item.title: Colombia’s president arrives at scene of supermarket hostage siege in tourist city
item.description:
Abelardo de la Espriella to take control of operation trying to free at least 20 hostages

Colombia’s president has arrived at the scene of an hours-long standoff between security services and gunmen holding at least 20 people hostage inside a supermarket in Cartagena, a popular tourist city.

Abelardo de la Espriella’s motorcade arrived in Cartagena on Tuesday night, Agence France-Presse reported, where he will ostensibly take control of an operation involving scores of officers, the navy and special forces.

item.title: ‘Once installed, there’s no getting rid of it’: what Falklands oil plans mean for its seals, whales and penguins
item.description:
While Argentina and the UK dispute sovereignty over the islands and its vast oil reserves, environmentalists fear for one of the Atlantic’s richest ecosystems

From the air, the main Falkland Islands form two large, jagged shapes against the South Atlantic. East Falkland and West Falkland are surrounded by 778 smaller islands and islets east of Patagonia’s southern tip.

The archipelago, a British overseas territory claimed by Argentina, is home to large colonies of albatrosses and penguins. Its waters, with those of the Patagonian shelf, provide feeding grounds for sea lions, southern elephant seals and southern right whales.
